source: One passively observed live production ingress to port 18082; not a generated smoke prompt

method.ingress_capture: Bounded tcpdump stream consumed in memory; first complete Codex Responses request only; stopped immediately afterwards
method.credential_headers: Authorization, cookies, API keys and forwarded client IPs removed before export
method.replay: Complete semantic JSON through the local production Forward path, using snapshots of two production client profiles and their independently probed egress zones; terminal upstream adapter captures the request and returns a fixture

preserved: turn_id, root_turn_id, context_window_id (observed unchanged across the two route replays)
original local filesystem paths, shell and workspace metadata
tool argument and output contents; 9 call/result associations
user and developer task instructions apart from the generated time blocks
identifier_policy_note: Turn/context IDs are still client-owned in the captured Desktop profile path. Account isolation of these IDs, if desired, needs deterministic mapping and consistent root/fork/prediction references; it is not equivalent to randomizing each request. Original session UUID inside a real workspace path must not be globally substituted.
timezone_semantics_note: The generated client time context explicitly tells the model to use it for user-facing dates and schedules. Rewriting it to the egress zone also changes that behavior; this is not merely transport fingerprint metadata.
limits: One real request; not representative of all clients or every request variant.
The complete outgoing body was inspected by an offline replay, not captured from the original production upstream TLS stream.
The small async-question metadata fix is local and is not included in the earlier deployed binary.
The captured payload is retained privately outside Git; the public report contains no prompt, workspace path or credential values.

tests.scope: async-question metadata regression, October metadata and Codex metadata tests
